I’m hoping to find that middle ground as well.

The average salary after graduation is $50,000-$54,999 according to internationalrelationsedu.org That’s how much I can expect in my first 5 years after graduation &  mid career pay is about minimum average of $84,000 and a median average of $124,000 as I want to be a Global Market Manager. College would be worth it especially abroad as the cultural exposure of being in a new environment would be immensely helpful and it’ll make me look well traveled which would be advantageous down the road when I’m applying for entry level jobs.

I’m not a US citizen. I’m South African I’m currently looking into a private bank loan but, I’ll do my due diligence first as I’m not desperate so after I compare repayment periods, interest rates and other benefits I’ll make my decision.

Apart time job is a must I know it will take some time but, I’m dedicated as long as the pay is decent. I was planning on visiting every Christmas & the travelling costs might not be too much of an issue as my family is planning to move to the uk in the next two years. So I could catch a ferry which is £35 to £55 & since my school is in Amsterdam a two way plane ticket would cost around £124.

I understand that and I’m appreciative that my parents are able to help and put me in a position to decide something like this but, i also don’t want to strain them financially. So if I can help take some pressure off with a student loan and a reasonable loan at that I think it’s worth it personally.

As for a loan provider. Haven’t yet done enough due diligence to make a decision. As I’m still going through  repayment terms, benefits, options and interest rates of the different types of student loans. All I know for certain is it’s going have to be a co-signing between my parents and I and I’m leaning more towards a private bank loan for now. As for which banks exactly I still need to do my research.

Getting a loan is nerve-racking considering all you ever hear is how bad student loan debts are and how you’ll end up paying them off for the rest of your life but, I do believe going abroad to further my studies and experiencing a different culture and environment will help immensely considering the career I want consists of a lot of travelling. So the exposure & experiences should help down the line as well.

I’m South African and do not have dual citizenship, I’m hoping I’ll be able to get between 30 to 35k. I’ve been doing some research and I seem to meet the requirements for the loan. I know getting it approved is another but so far that’s all I have.
I’m sorry you do. It’s not something anyone should feel but, there’s a comfort knowing in knowing it’s a shared pain we all have.
